LOS ANGELES, California (CNN) -- Michael Jackson knew "exactly how his fate would be played out" and feared his death would echo that of Elvis Presley, Lisa Marie Presley revealed in an online blog post published Friday morning.

Presley -- daughter of Elvis, the "King of Rock," and ex-wife of Jackson, the "King of Pop" -- wrote on her MySpace page that she wished "to say now what I have never said before because I want the truth out there for once." Her publicist confirmed that Presley authored the blog entry.

She stated that her brief marriage to Jackson -- spanning May 1994 to January 1996 -- "was not 'a sham,' as has been reported in the press," but explained that she divorced him because she found herself "in over my head" trying to save him "from the inevitable, which is what has just happened."

Presley recounted that Jackson had discussed his own death with her during "a deep conversation" some 14 years earlier, prompted by reflection on "the circumstances of my father's death."

"At some point he paused, he stared at me very intensely, and stated with an almost calm certainty, 'I am afraid that I am going to end up like him, the way he did,'" Presley wrote. "I promptly tried to deter him from the idea, at which point he simply shrugged his shoulders and nodded, almost matter-of-factly, as if to let me know that he knew what he knew, and that was that."

That exchange, she said, resurfaced vividly as she watched televised coverage of Jackson's death on Thursday.

"I am sitting here watching on the news [as] an ambulance leaves the driveway of his home, the big gates, the crowds outside the gates, the coverage, the crowds outside the hospital, the cause of death and what may have led up to it -- and the memory of this conversation hit me, as did the unstoppable tears," she wrote. "A predicted ending -- by him, by loved ones, and by me -- but what I didn't predict was how much it was going to hurt when it finally happened."

Elvis Presley collapsed in the bathroom of his Memphis, Tennessee, mansion, Graceland, on August 16, 1977, at the age of 42. Although his death was officially attributed to an irregular heartbeat, the autopsy report was sealed amid allegations that prescription drug abuse had contributed to the condition.

"As I sit here overwhelmed with sadness, reflection, and confusion at what was my biggest failure to date, watching on the news almost play by play the exact scenario I witnessed on August 16, 1977, unfold again with Michael -- a sight I never wanted to see again -- just as he predicted, I am truly, truly gutted," she wrote.

"I wanted to 'save him,'" she continued. "I wanted to save him from the inevitable, which is what has just happened."

"The hardest decision I have ever had to make was to walk away and let his fate have him, even though I desperately loved him and tried every way I could to stop or reverse it," Presley wrote.

She insisted that their marriage -- which some had dismissed as a mere publicity strategy to burnish Jackson's image -- was genuine.

"It was an unusual relationship, yes, where two unusual people who did not live or know a 'normal life' found a connection, perhaps with some suspect timing on his part," she wrote. "Nonetheless, I do believe he loved me as much as he could love anyone, and I loved him very much."

Presley described Jackson as "an incredibly dynamic force and power that was not to be underestimated."

"When he used it for something good, it was the best, and when he used it for something bad, it was really, REALLY bad," she wrote.

Presley's blog entry closed with gratitude toward her readers: "I really needed to say this right now. Thanks for listening."

Presley's blog can be found online at http://bit.ly/5wR7p.

# Los Angeles: The City of Angels

Los Angeles, California, stands as one of the most iconic and influential cities in the United States. Located along the Pacific coast in Southern California, LA is the second-most populous city in the country, home to nearly four million residents within its city limits and millions more throughout the greater metropolitan area.

## A Global Cultural Capital

Los Angeles is world-renowned as the heart of the entertainment industry. Hollywood, a district within the city, has become synonymous with filmmaking, television production, and the broader entertainment business. Major studios, production companies, and countless creative professionals call LA home, drawing aspiring actors, directors, writers, and musicians from around the globe who seek to make their mark in the industry.

## Geography and Climate

The city benefits from a Mediterranean climate characterized by warm, dry summers and mild winters, making outdoor activities enjoyable throughout much of the year. Los Angeles is nestled between mountains and the Pacific Ocean, offering residents and visitors access to diverse landscapes—from sandy beaches like Santa Monica and Venice to hiking trails in the Santa Monica Mountains and Griffith Park.

## Diversity and Culture

Los Angeles is remarkably diverse, with communities representing cultures from around the world. This diversity is reflected in the city's neighborhoods, cuisine, festivals, and daily life. Areas like Koreatown, Little Tokyo, Boyle Heights, and Chinatown showcase the rich multicultural fabric that defines the city's identity.

## Economic Significance

Beyond entertainment, California's largest city serves as a major hub for technology, international trade, fashion, and business. The Port of Los Angeles ranks among the busiest in the nation, facilitating significant international commerce. Silicon Beach, the area's growing tech scene, has attracted numerous startups and established tech companies alike.

## Challenges and Character

Like many major urban centers, Los Angeles faces challenges including traffic congestion, housing affordability, and environmental concerns. Despite these issues, the city continues to attract people with its promise of opportunity, its sunny disposition, and its unique blend of urban sophistication and laid-back California culture.

Los Angeles remains a place where dreams are pursued, cultures blend, and innovation thrives—truly earning its reputation as one of America's most dynamic cities.
